title: Sable and the Garden
premise: Cyrus Underhill, a scribe indentured to the Temple of Quiet Hours, lives in a valley where magic cannot cross its borders — the only place the sold and stolen can hide. When a dying courier named Sable presses a blood-inked map into his hands, Cyrus learns his own soul was collateral on a debt his father never paid, held by the court beneath Mount Vael. To reclaim it before the last dragon-fire gutters out and the valley's protection dies with it, he must leave everything safe behind, barter with memory-eating brokers, and confront the truth that Sable is not a stranger but the remnant of who Cyrus was meant to be. In the end, Cyrus chooses to split himself: one soul returned to the mountain to free every debtor, one kept in the valley — whole enough to live, changed forever.
about_author: Rafael Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debt ledgers from defunct monasteries, an experience that haunts every page of this book. They write fantasy about paperwork, grief, and the small mercies people trade away.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Cyrus copies temple ledgers under a master who counts his breaths, establishing his debt-bound life and the valley's strange stillness where magic cannot follow. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet suffocation, the ache of a life already mortgaged.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gatehouse
chapters.summary: A bleeding woman collapses at the valley's border stone, half-dissolved as if the land itself rejects her. She presses a map inked in blood into Cyrus's hands and whispers that his name is written beneath the mountain. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror disguised as duty.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Cyrus searches the temple archives and finds his father's contract: a soul pledged as surety, renewed yearly — until this year, when no one paid. The abbot knows, and has been hiding it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised him.

chapters.title: Crossing the Stone
chapters.summary: Fleeing temple guards who want the map destroyed, Cyrus steps over the border stone for the first time. Magic floods him like cold water; the world sharpens, and so do his fears. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: vertigo and terrible freedom.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Debts
chapters.summary: On the pilgrim road, Cyrus meets Wren, a tinker who pays her way with traded memories, and learns how souls are currency outside the valley. He hides the map even from her. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: wary first trust.

chapters.title: The Broker of Ashford Market
chapters.summary: In a market town, a memory-broker offers to read the map for a price: one hour of Cyrus's childhood. He pays, and sees his father's face clearly for the first time in years. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief purchased willingly.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: The map begins speaking in Sable's voice, guiding Cyrus through a dead forest. She reveals fragments: she was a courier who failed, and something of her remains bound to the ink. POV: alternating Cyrus and Sable's residual consciousness. Emotional beat: loneliness finding company.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren is caught selling a stolen memory to a dragon-cult scout; Cyrus buys her freedom with the broker's hour of childhood. She swears a debt to him — the first kindness anyone has owed him. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into loyalty.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: From a ridge, they see Mount Vael: a fortress-city carved inside, lit by the guttering last dragon-fire that powers all soul-contracts. Its light visibly dims. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread at the scale of what owns him.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: Posing as a debt-clerk, Cyrus infiltrates the outer court using his genuine scribe skills. He finds the registry of souls — and his own entry, annotated in his father's handwriting: 'forgive me.' POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the past made physical.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Cyrus witnesses the dragon-fire ceremony: the last dragon, ancient and lucid, burning itself as fuel for the court's contracts. When it dies, every soul-debt becomes forfeit — including his. POV: the dragon, Ember-of-the-Long-Vigil. Emotional beat: compassion for the jailer.

chapters.title: A Debt Collector Named Mercy
chapters.summary: The court's chief collector, Lady Asche, catches Cyrus but offers a deal: betray the map's purpose and she'll forgive his debt. He refuses — and doesn't know why until later. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: integrity discovered by accident.

chapters.title: Sable's Confession
chapters.summary: The map finally speaks plainly: Sable was Cyrus — or rather, the version of him the court took at birth, sent back as a courier, and destroyed when she tried to warn him. His identity was split to secure the original loan. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: selfhood revealed as theft.

chapters.title: Wren Walks Away
chapters.summary: Learning Cyrus intends to dissolve all contracts — erasing debts Wren relies on to survive — she leaves in fury. Cyrus must decide whether liberation imposed on others is just another kind of ownership. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: righteous anger, real moral cost.

chapters.title: The Registry Vault
chapters.summary: With Ember's secret help — the dragon wants an end more than anyone — Cyrus breaches the vault holding the master ledger. But the ledger is alive, woven from stolen memories, and it recognizes him. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: horror and recognition intertwined.

chapters.title: Lady Asche's Price
chapters.summary: Asche corners him in the vault and reveals her own soul was the first ever pledged; freeing everyone frees nothing for her. She demands Cyrus take her place as keeper of the ledger. POV: Asche. Emotional beat: the villain as the story's oldest victim.

chapters.title: When the Fire Goes Out
chapters.summary: Ember's flame gutters to embers mid-negotiation. Across the mountain, contracts begin collapsing; debtors convulse as their souls are recalled raw. Chaos erupts through the court. POV: multiple, braided. Emotional beat: catastrophe as consequence of delay.

chapters.title: The Choice of Two Souls
chapters.summary: At the heart of the vault, Cyrus learns the truth of the ending: one soul can anchor the ledger kindly, or two can unmake it entirely — but only if both halves consent. He asks Sable what she wants. POV: Cyrus and Sable together. Emotional beat: love between the divided self.

chapters.title: What Sable Wanted
chapters.summary: Sable chooses dissolution — not death, but return: her fragment will seed the new ledger so it remembers mercy instead of arithmetic. Her farewell is the book's emotional summit. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief that is also gratitude.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: Cyrus, Wren (returned), and Ember's final breath unmake the old ledger. Souls stream home across the valley and beyond; Asche, freed after centuries, weeps at her own name. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: release on a mythic scale.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Changed
chapters.summary: Magic now crosses the border stone freely, and the valley must learn to live without its walls. Cyrus returns to the temple not as debtor but as witness, carrying Sable's memories alongside his own. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: bittersweet integration.

chapters.title: The Garden
chapters.summary: Epilogue: years later, Cyrus tends a garden over the old border stone where names are planted instead of debts. A child asks who Sable was. 'Someone I was,' he says, 'and someone I got to meet.' POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept.
